answer.why_different: The difference is primarily structural: the generated document adds the notification-target path that is absent from the official side. However, the generated operation also contains a semantic value/reference mismatch: operationId `notifyMoiCreation` is paired with `NotifyMoiAttributeValueChanges` instead of the creation notification schema.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP specification defines `{notificationTarget}` as a resource whose POST operation sends notifications. It also states that `NotifyMOICreation` is the request-body type for `notifyMOICreation`, whereas `NotifyMoiAttributeValueChanges` is a different notification type.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 permits a templated path such as `/{notificationTarget}` and defines a POST operation on a Path Item Object. The generated path therefore has a valid OpenAPI address and structure, but its request-body schema does not match its creation operation.
answer.clearer_why: The generated document exposes the notification-target endpoint, which is absent from the official side, so it is more informative to an API reader. Nevertheless, the mismatched request-body reference makes the generated endpoint misleading and must be corrected.

### Relative References in URLs  
Unless specified otherwise, all properties that are URLs MAY be relative references as defined by [RFC3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-4.2).
Relative references are resolved using the URLs defined in the [`Server Object`](#server-object) as a Base URI.  
Relative references used in `$ref` are processed as per [JSON Reference](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-pbryan-zyp-json-ref-03), using the URL of the current document as the base URI. See also the [Reference Object](#reference-object).

#### Parameter Object  
Describes a single operation parameter.  
A unique parameter is defined by a combination of a [name](#parameterName) and [location](#parameterIn).  
##### Parameter Locations
There are four possible parameter locations specified by the `in` field:
* path - Used together with [Path Templating](#path-templating), where the parameter value is actually part of the operation's URL. This does not include the host or base path of the API. For example, in `/items/{itemId}`, the path parameter is `itemId`.
* query - Parameters that are appended to the URL. For example, in `/items?id=###`, the query parameter is `id`.
* header - Custom headers that are expected as part of the request. Note that [RFC7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#page-22) states header names are case insensitive.
* cookie - Used to pass a specific cookie value to the API.
